name: Nostoi
tagline: Bring the record home. Make changes to history visible.
description: Nostoi helps people inspect the integrity of an audit trail. It verifies linked records, locates the first break, and supports checkpoints kept beyond the system whose story is being checked.
status: Active development · chain tools and bindings available in source
motifCaption: The homecoming: a chain carried safely across the river.

highlights.label: Integrity
highlights.title: Find the first inconsistent record
highlights.text: Verify JSON Lines and supported SQLite chains. A broken chain is reported, rather than quietly extended.

highlights.label: Perspective
highlights.title: Keep a head outside the story
highlights.text: A retained external checkpoint helps reveal a removed tail or recomputed history that local hash links alone cannot detect.

highlights.label: Clear questions
highlights.title: A signature is not a test result
highlights.text: Integrity, signer identity and independent observation answer different questions. Keep each claim understandable.

sections.title: A record should survive the people and processes that made it.
paragraphs: Nostoi is RAGBAZ’s Rust library, CLI and terminal interface for audit chains. It can verify, append, stream and browse records; verification identifies the first inconsistency instead of reducing the whole history to a reassuring green badge.

It reads nostoi-v1 chains used by projects such as Frog and Sylvae, WeftMark’s ledger format, and Ephor’s audit-store format. The portable core is separated from networking, Linux-specific ingestion and interactive tools.
The name means homecomings. Its duckling carries Gretel across the river: an image of helping a fragile story reach another person intact.

sections.title: Tamper-evident is a useful promise. Tamper-proof would be the wrong one.
paragraphs: Hash links can expose a changed record within a chain. Someone who controls the whole file may still remove its tail or recompute the entire history. Detecting that requires a previously trusted head retained elsewhere.

External checkpoints, replication and multi-destination anchoring improve the situation. Separate administrations can offer different witnesses. They do not abolish the need to choose who and what you trust.
Signed attestations say which key signed a statement under a verification policy. The signer’s claimed time, another party’s observation time and a passing test remain separate facts.

sections.title: Useful for teams that need to explain, not merely assert.
paragraphs: A team can inspect whether its agent-run audit log remains internally consistent. A reviewer can retain a checkpoint with engineering evidence. An operator can keep an audit replica separate from the runtime that generated it.

With Sylvae, this supports the integrity of a run trail. With WeftMark, it complements the explanation of code changes. Rebekah supplies a home for the tools, while Ephor remains the separate governance authority when enabled.
Keep signing keys with their operators. A public project website does not need your private key or raw private audit log to explain these ideas.

sections.title: Trust is stronger when it admits its limits.
paragraphs: Fear about dangerous AI or harmful human uses of AI cannot be answered by a logo or a checksum alone. Nostoi provides one inspectable layer: the integrity of the recorded story and its retained checkpoints.

RAGBAZ’s broader intention is benevolent cooperation. A careful record can help people challenge an unsupported claim, learn from a mistake and continue a project without depending on one powerful actor’s memory.

That value extends beyond software. We want accountable work to be affordable and understandable, while being honest that these tools do not by themselves resolve alignment, existential risk, legal responsibility or the truth of every recorded statement.

workflow.title: Choose a chain you understand
workflow.text: Identify the producer, format and purpose. A chain of events is not automatically a chain of true claims.

workflow.title: Verify before trusting the next record
workflow.text: Use Nostoi to locate any break. Treat an unreadable file, bad input and an inconsistent chain as distinct outcomes.

workflow.title: Retain an external checkpoint
workflow.text: Keep a verified head beyond the producer’s reach. Where the stakes warrant it, use independently administered destinations.

workflow.title: Bring integrity into human review
workflow.text: Attach the checkpoint or attestation to the wider evidence story. Keep signer trust and engineering readiness distinct.

quickstart.title: Make a small chain and inspect it
quickstart.summary: Build the CLI from source with a working Rust toolchain, then create a harmless local example before working with operational records.
quickstart.note: Registry publication is pending. External anchoring, signatures and trusted signer policy need their own deliberate setup.

commands.label: Build the CLI
commands.code:
git clone https://github.com/tabenius/nostoi.git
cd nostoi
cargo build --release --bin nostoi

commands.label: Create and verify a local example
commands.code:
./target/release/nostoi append example.jsonl \
  --kind example.start --body '{"purpose":"learning"}'
./target/release/nostoi verify example.jsonl
./target/release/nostoi head example.jsonl

pages.title: Three questions behind a trustworthy audit trail
pages.description: Integrity, signer trust and external observation are useful precisely because they are not the same claim.

sections.title: Did the recorded sequence change?
paragraphs: Verify the chain before appending or acting on it. The first inconsistent record tells you where the evidence about continuity stops.
A fully recomputed history or removed tail can evade an internal-only check. Compare against a previously retained external head.

sections.title: Who signed this statement?
paragraphs: A valid signature binds a statement to a key. Your policy still determines whether that key is trusted, and for which purpose.
Do not treat an unverified key label or the existence of a sidecar file as evidence that a signature was checked.

sections.title: When did somebody else observe it?
paragraphs: A signer can choose a timestamp in their own statement. Independent observation adds another record, with its own source and time.
The resulting evidence can support a WeftMark review or an operator’s incident investigation. It cannot prove that every statement in the underlying chain is true.
